data.name: Anti Gravity Warriors VR
data.detailed_description:
Fight alien space robots and mutant monsters in this immersive, Sci-Fi, zero gravity environment. Battle to the death in this vr game! This game include three levels and complex gameplay. Fight various types of enemys while trying to complete objectives.

Key Features

  • A shield
  • Exploding robots
  • Maze-Like Levels
  • Exploding robots
  • Doors that can be opened
  • Exploding robots
  • Save Games
  • And finnaly, exploding robots

reviews.review:
Anti Gravity Warriors VR is a compact science-fiction action experience that represents the experimental spirit of the earlier years of consumer virtual reality. Developed and published by Niket Patel, the game places the player inside a hostile zero-gravity environment filled with alien robots, mutant creatures, enclosed corridors, and objectives that must be completed while surviving enemy encounters. Rather than attempting to deliver a lengthy campaign, it focuses on a small collection of mechanics designed specifically around VR, resulting in an experience that is easy to understand but noticeably limited in scale.

The zero-gravity theme is the element that gives the game most of its identity. Movement through its science-fiction environments feels considerably different from exploring an ordinary first-person shooter, while the maze-like level design encourages players to pay attention to their surroundings instead of simply moving from one firefight to another. Doors can be opened to gain access to additional areas, and objectives provide some direction through the otherwise compact environments. There are only three levels, however, so players should expect a short adventure rather than an expansive campaign. The environments provide enough structure for exploration, but the limited number of stages means the novelty carries much of the experience.

Combat is deliberately uncomplicated. Players encounter several kinds of enemies, including robots and mutant monsters, while a shield adds a defensive option during confrontations. The developers clearly wanted exploding robots to be one of the game's defining attractions, and destruction provides much of the immediate arcade satisfaction. There is something amusingly straightforward about entering a zero-gravity environment and destroying mechanical opponents without having to learn elaborate character builds, skill trees, inventories, or complicated combat systems. This simplicity makes the action accessible, although it also means encounters can begin feeling repetitive after the basic mechanics become familiar.

The maze-like layouts add some welcome exploration between battles. Searching for the correct route and figuring out how to reach objectives gives the player something to consider beyond shooting whatever appears nearby. A save-game feature is also included, which is useful even for such a relatively short experience. These individual mechanics are fairly basic when considered separately, but together they create a functional mixture of navigation, combat, environmental interaction, and objective completion. The game works best when treated as an experimental VR action title rather than something intended to compete with larger and considerably more sophisticated virtual reality releases.

Presentation is where its age and independent origins are most apparent. Released in 2017, Anti Gravity Warriors VR comes from a period when developers were still heavily experimenting with what worked in room-scale and standing VR. Its visual design and overall level of refinement therefore feel modest compared with more recent VR productions. It does not offer an elaborate narrative presentation or a particularly deep world to investigate. Instead, its science-fiction atmosphere mainly exists to support the combat and zero-gravity premise. Players who enjoy older VR experiments may find this simplicity interesting, while anyone expecting the production values of a modern VR shooter will probably find it dated.

Its free-to-play status helps compensate for the small amount of content. With no purchase price required, the three-level structure is easier to accept as a short curiosity. The hardware requirements are also modest by modern gaming standards, with the original minimum specification listing hardware around an Intel Core i5-4590 or AMD FX-8350, 6 GB of RAM, and a GTX 960 or Radeon R9 290. It requires SteamVR and is specifically designed as a VR-only experience with tracked controller support and standing or room-scale play.

Steam Deck compatibility is Unsupported for practical purposes because this is a VR-only SteamVR game. Steam Deck does not provide the required native VR environment for playing it as intended, so this should not be considered a portable Deck title. Players interested in the game should instead approach it with a compatible Windows PC and SteamVR hardware. This distinction is particularly important because there is no conventional non-VR mode that could simply be played using the Steam Deck's built-in controls and display.

Anti Gravity Warriors VR ultimately succeeds more as an interesting piece of early independent VR experimentation than as a substantial action game. The zero-gravity setting, shield mechanic, maze-like environments, objective-driven progression, mutant enemies, and plentiful exploding robots give it enough personality to separate it from completely generic shooting experiences. Its major weakness is simply that there is not enough of it. Three levels and relatively straightforward mechanics restrict its longevity, while its age is increasingly noticeable. As a free and unusual VR diversion, however, it can still provide some entertainment for players interested in exploring lesser-known titles from SteamVR's earlier period.

Rating: 6/10
